positions.name: SoloOperatorB2CPositioning
positions.frame: How should go-to-market positioning balance individual solo operators against top-tier enterprise deployments?
positions.why: Tina argues for treating solo builders operating with multiple AI tools as their own complete teams, which Tanya adopts as a shift toward a direct B2C bottom tier beneath an enterprise tier.

positions.name: TargetCustomerKnowledgeProfile
positions.frame: How should target customer qualification distinguish non-tech knowledge organizations from developer teams with bespoke tooling?
positions.why: Xavier advises targeting organizations that operate on knowledge without identifying as tech companies, noting alongside Tanya that technical builders resist adoption because they build their own fragmented solutions.

attaches.why: Xavier and Tanya explore whether defensibility stems from proprietary graph manipulation over customer data or cross-organizational network positioning where counterparties both use the product.
Freya articulates how applying an expert's personal lens is the irreducible unique component that prevents AI output from breaking.
Tanya reaffirms the core technical differentiator of extracting citable perspective from textual documents and notes delivering perspectives as deck alternatives remains the strategic future.
Tanya describes building marketplace inventory by interviewing experts on a podcast and converting each conversation into an installable perspective.
Freya states the core sales dynamic that human emotional moments drive conversion over textual proof.
